title: Sir Patrick Stewart, Legendary 'Star Trek' Captain and 'X-Men' Icon, Dies at 86
snippet: Sir Patrick Stewart, the revered Shakespearean actor who achieved global stardom as Captain Jean-Luc Picard and Professor Charles Xavier, has passed away at the age of 86.
content:
Sir Patrick Stewart, the commanding British actor whose legendary career spanned six decades across classical theater, television, and blockbuster cinema, has died. He was 86.

According to an official statement released on his social media accounts, Stewart passed away peacefully at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday, surrounded by his wife, Sunny Ozell, along with close family and friends. His death followed a struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.

"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," the family statement read, highlighting his "invincible grace" and indelible contributions to the arts.

From Stratford to Starfleet

Born on July 13, 1940, in Mirfield, Yorkshire, England, Stewart dropped out of school at age 15 to work at a local newspaper before pursuing formal drama training in 1957. He joined the prestigious Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966, establishing himself as one of Britain's most formidable classical stage actors.

In the mid-1980s, Stewart made a fateful transition to Hollywood when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation. Running from 1987 to 1994, the series turned Stewart into a global household name. He went on to headline four Star Trek feature films and recently reprised his iconic role in the Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard.

In 2000, Stewart captured a new generation of superhero fans as Professor Charles Xavier in 20th Century Fox's X-Men, a role he portrayed across multiple films over two decades, including the acclaimed 2017 blockbuster Logan.

A Legacy Beyond the Screen

Beyond his iconic screen presence, Stewart was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010 for his contributions to television, film, and theater. He was also known for his extensive philanthropic work, advocating tirelessly for domestic violence survivors, human rights, military veterans' mental health, and animal rescue organizations.

Tributes quickly began pouring in from around the entertainment world following the news. His long-time friend and X-Men co-star Hugh Jackman posted an emotional remembrance online, writing, "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."

Stewart is survived by his wife, Sunny Ozell, whom he married in 2013, and two adult children, Daniel and Sophie, from his first marriage.
